README.md:78:| `trigger_phrase` | Text that starts pi. The match ignores case | No | `@pi` |
README.md:86:| `thinking_level` | How much the model thinks before it answers: `off`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, or `max`. A model that does not support the level gets the nearest level that it supports, and a model without reasoning support gets `off` (see [Thinking](docs/models.md#thinking)) | No | `medium` |
README.md:92:| `model_reasoning` | The custom model supports reasoning (thinking). When `false`, the model gets `thinking_level: off` | No | `false` |
README.md:118:- `extensions`, `skills`, `exclude_tools`, `model_tools_hidden`, and `worktree_snapshot_exclude` accept commas and new lines. pi-action ignores empty lines and `#` comments: a full line, or the rest of a line after a spec and a space.
docs/workflows.md:18:To allow only some users, set `allowed_users`. When it is set, pi-action ignores `allowed_associations`:
docs/workflows.md:36:To allow bots such as Dependabot or Renovate, add their logins to `allowed_bots`. pi-action ignores bots that are not in this list:
docs/how-it-works.md:18:1. **Find the request** ([`src/run-context.ts`](../src/run-context.ts)). The request is `pr_number`, or a direct `prompt`, or the event. An event can be a new issue or pull request, a comment, or an answer to a question. pi-action ignores an event without the trigger phrase, and edits of comments other than questions.
docs/extensions.md:8:Both kinds can also give **prompt templates** (`pi.prompts`) and **skills** (`pi.skills`, or a `skills/` directory). See [Prompts](prompts.md#prompt-templates) and [Skills](skills.md). A package with only skills can go in the `skills` input instead, which does not run its code.
docs/extensions.md:14:Write one extension per line, or separate them with commas. pi-action ignores empty lines and `#` comments. A comment can be a full line, or it can follow a spec after a space. The `#` in a git ref such as `github:owner/repo#v1.0.0` is not a comment, because no space comes before it:
docs/extensions.md:59:pi-action ignores these parts of a pi extension and writes a warning to the log:
docs/extensions.md:115:`trust_project` (default `false`) tells the extension that it can load and run the configuration of the repository. For pit, this is `.pi/pit.json` and `.pi/functions`. pi-action uses it too: for the prompt templates in `.pi/prompts`, the skills in `.pi/skills` and `.agents/skills`, and `.pi/SYSTEM.md` and `.pi/APPEND_SYSTEM.md` (see [Security](security.md#skills-from-the-repository)).
docs/extensions.md:161:The workflow must listen to `issue_comment` `edited` events. Its `if:` filter must let these events and `/answer` replies through. Use the workflow of the [quick start](../README.md#quick-start). pi-action ignores edits of other comments.
docs/extensions.md:171:- For `confirm` and `select`, the first box that you tick is the answer. pi-action ignores ticks on a question that has an answer.
docs/skills.md:14:1. **Packages.** Each package in `extensions`, then each package in `skills`, in the order of the input: the `pi.skills` list in its `package.json` (files and directories, as `pi.prompts`), or else its `skills/` directory.
docs/models.md:100:`thinking_level` sets how much the model thinks (reasons) before it answers. The default is `medium`, as in pi. A higher level can give better answers to difficult tasks, but it uses more tokens and more time. To turn thinking off, set `off`:
docs/models.md:104:  thinking_level: off   # or minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max
docs/models.md:108:- **Models that support less.** pi-action caps the level as pi does (pi-ai's `clampThinkingLevel`), and writes a log line, for example `thinking_level: openai/gpt-4o has no reasoning support; using off`:
docs/prompts.md:69:3. **Nested files** below the working directory (for example `packages/api/AGENTS.md`) are not loaded. The section lists their paths (up to 20, one for each directory) and tells pi to read the one for the directory where it works. pi-action finds them with `git ls-files`, so it ignores the files that git ignores.
docs/prompts.md:85:A thread from an earlier version of pi-action, with the old `# Project Context` layout, gets one `Updated system prompt section "project_context"` in its next run.
docs/prompts.md:115:The **task** is the text after the first occurrence of the trigger phrase, without spaces at the start and end. The match ignores case. For `@pi please review this`, the task is `please review this`.
docs/prompts.md:129:1. The `pi.prompts` files and directories of each package in `extensions`, in the order of the input. This includes packages with a pi-durable extension.
docs/prompts.md:130:2. `.pi/prompts/*.md` in the repository, **only with `trust_project: true`**. See [Security](security.md#prompt-templates-from-the-repository).
docs/prompts.md:176:`prompt_template` replaces the **complete** built-in first message. pi-action does not add the requirements block to your template. If you want pi to commit and push its work, write this in your template.
docs/security.md:31:- The sender of the event has the `write`, `maintain`, or `admin` role (from `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/collaborators/{user}/permission`). If the check fails, pi-action ignores the tick.
docs/security.md:79:A [prompt template](prompts.md#prompt-templates) becomes the request of the user. Anyone who can push a branch can change the files in `.pi/prompts`. Thus, pi-action loads them only with `trust_project: true`. Without it, pi-action writes `Not loading the prompt templates in .pi/prompts: trust_project is off` to the log. Templates from `extensions` and from `agent_dir` load in all cases.
docs/threads.md:62:- Files that git ignores (`.gitignore`, `.git/info/exclude`), for example `node_modules`, build output, or an ignored `.env`.
src/extensions.ts:62:	/** Each package's `pi.prompts`, in input order. */
src/extensions.ts:222:/** pi's manifest entries (`pi.extensions`, `pi.prompts`): paths and globs, with `!` globs excluding matches. */
src/extensions.ts:253:/** The paths of a `pi` manifest list (`pi.prompts`, `pi.skills`); undefined when the package has no such list. */
src/extensions.ts:264:/** A package's prompt templates (`pi.prompts`: files and directories), under its name; undefined without any. */
src/extensions.ts:411: * extension can do in the coding agent (tools, commands, event handlers, UI) is ignored with a warning,
src/extensions.ts:575: * Loads one installed package or path: its prompt templates (`pi.prompts`), and its pi-durable extension when it
src/prompts.ts:10:	/** Shown in the log: a package name, `.pi/prompts`, or `agent_dir`. */
src/prompts.ts:69:					`Prompt template /${name} from ${source} is ignored: ${taken.source} has one with that name`,
src/run.ts:123:/** The prompt templates of the run: the extensions' `pi.prompts`, then `.pi/prompts`, then `<agent_dir>/prompts`. */
src/run.ts:134:				{ source: ".pi/prompts", dirs: [".pi/prompts"] },
src/skills.ts:229:					`Skill ${name} from ${source} is ignored: ${taken.source} has one with that name`,
src/thread.ts:460: * `requested`, capped as pi caps it to what the model supports (pi-ai's `clampThinkingLevel`): `off` for a model
.
